draft.title: Voyages of discovery
card: From the late 1400s, European sailors set out to find sea routes to Asia. Asia was the source of spices, silk and other goods that sold for high prices in Europe.
In 1492, Christopher Columbus sailed west from Spain, hoping to reach Asia. He reached islands in the Caribbean, in the Americas, which were unknown to most Europeans.
In 1498, Vasco da Gama of Portugal sailed around the southern tip of Africa and reached India by sea.
The voyages began a new age of contact between Europe and other parts of the world. Contact often led to conquest, as European powers took land and control from the people who already lived there.
draft.remember: Europeans sought sea routes to Asia's riches, and the voyages brought lasting contact and conquest.

a.q: Why did European sailors such as Columbus and da Gama make their voyages?
opts: To find sea routes to the riches of Asia
To spread the Silk Road across central Asia
To escape the fall of the Roman Empire
To find new lands for the Pope to rule
a.why: The sailors wanted sea routes to Asia, where goods such as spices and silk were sold at high prices in Europe. Finding new lands to conquer came later, as a result of contact, and was not the aim of these voyages.
a.clue: Think about where spices and silk came from.

b.q: Columbus sailed west from Spain in 1492 and reached islands in the Caribbean. What best describes what he had found?
opts: Lands in the Americas, not the Asia he had aimed for
A sea route around Africa to the coast of India
A part of Asia that Europeans already traded with
A trade route that replaced the overland Silk Road
b.why: Columbus aimed for Asia but reached the Americas, which were unknown to most Europeans. The route around Africa to India was da Gama's, which is the most tempting wrong answer.
b.clue: Which voyage went around Africa, and which went west?

a.best: To find sea routes to the riches of Asia

b.best: Lands in the Americas, not the Asia he had aimed for

problems.detail: The why says finding new lands to conquer 'was not the aim' of these voyages. That overstates it, and the card does not teach it. Columbus's 1492 agreement with the Spanish Crown already made him viceroy and governor of any lands he found. Soften this to say that reaching Asia's riches was the main aim.
